To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new particle resolved numerical method for simulating interphase momentum transfer, and used this method to study gas-solid momentum transfer in flow through a packed bed of monodisperme spheres.

(a) the drag law for monodispersed gas solid flow can be accurately predicted using DNS of flow past fixed particle assemblies, and (b) the pressure contribution to the drag law is linearly dependent on the Reynolds number, while the viscous contribution varies non linearly with Rem.

the average drag on a particle is reconcilable (consistent) with the two fluid theory for the first time, that the drag is not linear in Rem for Rem 100, and that an improved correlation for the average drag has been proposed that is more accurate than previously reported correlations for Rem 100 300, ph 0.1 0.5.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a consistent and accurate numerical method for studying the interphase momentum transfer problem in gas solid flows.
the numerical solution of fluid particle interaction problems using a particle resolved DNS approach that is consistent with the averaged two-fluid equations.
developing a new numerical method for simulating interphase momentum transfer, and using this numerical method to study the drag law for monodispersed gas solid systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our DNS results are more accurate and extendable to higher Reynolds number and volume fraction than previous DNS results, and that the improved drag law proposed herein is more accurate than existing drag laws for the Reynolds number range 100 500.
our DNS of interphase momentum transport in monodisperse fixed bed assemblies of spheres is the most accurate to date and that the drag law we infer from these simulations is the best to date.
the drag law for fixed monodisperse assemblies is a function of the mean slip velocity, the mean slip velocity being a function of the solid volume fraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the drag law proposed here for the first time provides a good approximation for F in the entire range of ph and Rem considered in this study.

we present a consistent DNS approach for simulating gas solid flow that yields drag values in good agreement with the average two fluid theory and we propose an improved drag correlation for the range of Rem and ph studied in this work.
we have demonstrated the ability of a new numerical method (PUReIBM), which is based on the immersed boundary method (IBM) to simulate interphase momentum transfer for a wide range of ph and Rem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
particle resolved DNS simulations can be a powerful tool for studying gas solid momentum transfer, and the results of such simulations can be used to improve existing drag correlations.
the drag law is not universal, but rather depends on the flow conditions, the particle size distribution, the particle geometry, the particle surface properties and other factors.
the accuracy of the average two fluid drag law is dependent on the accuracy of the numerical method.
